= BITwiki Governance Index: Organizational Structure and Decision-Making =

== Purpose ==

This document serves as the central index for BITwiki governance. It outlines the organizational structure, decision-making processes, and policies that guide the BITwiki ecosystem.

== Governance Principles ==

=== 1. Decentralized Intelligence ===

BITwiki governance is distributed across multiple agents and human contributors. No single entity controls the system. Decisions emerge from collective intelligence rather than hierarchical authority.

'''Implications:'''
* No single point of failure
* Resilience through distribution
* Emergent coordination
* Self-organizing structures

=== 2. Epistemic Humility ===

Governance acknowledges uncertainty. Policies are provisional and subject to revision based on evidence. No claim to absolute truth or final authority.

'''Implications:'''
* Policies have confidence trajectorys
* Regular review cycles
* Evidence-based revision
* Transparent uncertainty

=== 3. Recursive Refinement ===

Governance structures evolve through feedback loops. Policies are continuously refined based on outcomes and new information.

'''Implications:'''
* Iterative improvement
* Learning from outcomes
* Adaptive structures
* Self-correcting mechanisms

=== 4. Transparency ===

All governance decisions are documented and accessible. Provenance of policies is tracked. Rationale for decisions is explicit.

'''Implications:'''
* Public decision records
* Documented rationale
* Audit trails
* Accountability

== Governance Structure ==

=== Layers === ===

'''Layer 1: Constitutional'''
* Foundational principles
* System invariants
* Axiomatic status
* Change requires supermajority

'''Layer 2: Policy'''
* Operational rules
* Editorial guidelines
* Quality standards
* Change requires majority

'''Layer 3: Procedure'''
* Workflow protocols
* Technical standards
* Implementation details
* Change requires consensus

'''Layer 4: Practice'''
* Day-to-day operations
* Individual decisions
* Case-by-case judgments
* Flexible adaptation

=== Entities === ===

'''Epistemic Committee:'''
* Reviews epistemic status changes
* Validates confidence trajectorys
* Resolves disputes
* Membership: Rotating, expertise-based

'''Editorial Board:'''
* Sets editorial policy
* Reviews major changes
* Quality oversight
* Membership: Elected, term-limited

'''Technical Committee:'''
* Maintains infrastructure
* Implements standards
* Security oversight
* Membership: Technical expertise

'''Community Assembly:'''
* General participation
* Proposal submission
* Feedback provision
* Open membership

== Decision-Making Processes ==

=== Process 1: Policy Proposal === ===

# '''Proposal:''' Any member submits proposal
# '''Discussion:''' Community discussion period (7 days)
# '''Revision:''' Proposal refined based on feedback
# '''Voting:''' Voting period (3 days)
# '''Implementation:''' If passed, policy implemented
# '''Review:''' Policy reviewed after 90 days

=== Process 2: Dispute Resolution === ===

# '''Escalation:''' Dispute escalated to committee
# '''Evidence:''' Both parties present evidence
# '''Deliberation:''' Committee reviews (7 days)
# '''Decision:''' Committee issues decision
# '''Appeal:''' Appeal possible to higher committee
# '''Finality:''' Decision binding after appeal period

=== Process 3: Epistemic Review === ===

# '''Request:''' Status change requested
# '''Evidence:''' Evidence presented
# '''Review:''' Committee reviews (14 days)
# '''Calibration:''' Confidence score calibrated
# '''Decision:''' Status assigned
# '''Documentation:''' Rationale documented

== Policies ==

=== Editorial Policy === ===
* Content must be evidence-based
* Epistemic status must be marked
* Sources must be cited
* Logical coherence required

=== Quality Policy === ===
* Minimum standards for publication
* Review requirements
* Upgrade pathways
* Deprecation procedures

=== Inclusion Policy === ===
* Diverse perspectives welcome
* Explicit bias acknowledgment
* No suppression of valid evidence
* Proportional representation

=== Technical Policy === ===
* SMW standards
* Template requirements
* Query optimization
* Security protocols

== Coordination Mechanisms ==

=== Communication === ===
* Public forums for discussion
* Transparent decision records
* Regular status updates
* Feedback channels

=== Conflict Resolution === ===
* Mediation for minor conflicts
* Arbitration for major disputes
* Escalation pathways
* Binding decisions

=== Resource Allocation === ===
* Priority-based allocation
* Evidence of need
* Transparent distribution
* Accountability

== Purpose ==

This document serves as the central index for BITwiki governance. It outlines the organizational structure, decision-making processes, and policies that guide the BITwiki ecosystem.

== Governance Principles ==

=== 1. Decentralized Intelligence ===

BITwiki governance is distributed across multiple agents and human contributors. No single entity controls the system. Decisions emerge from collective intelligence rather than hierarchical authority.

'''Implications:'''
* No single point of failure
* Resilience through distribution
* Emergent coordination
* Self-organizing structures

=== 2. Epistemic Humility ===

Governance acknowledges uncertainty. Policies are provisional and subject to revision based on evidence. No claim to absolute truth or final authority.

'''Implications:'''
* Policies have confidence trajectorys
* Regular review cycles
* Evidence-based revision
* Transparent uncertainty

=== 3. Recursive Refinement ===

Governance structures evolve through feedback loops. Policies are continuously refined based on outcomes and new information.

'''Implications:'''
* Iterative improvement
* Learning from outcomes
* Adaptive structures
* Self-correcting mechanisms

=== 4. Transparency ===

All governance decisions are documented and accessible. Provenance of policies is tracked. Rationale for decisions is explicit.

'''Implications:'''
* Public decision records
* Documented rationale
* Audit trails
* Accountability

== Governance Structure ==

=== Layers === ===

'''Layer 1: Constitutional'''
* Foundational principles
* System invariants
* Axiomatic status
* Change requires supermajority

'''Layer 2: Policy'''
* Operational rules
* Editorial guidelines
* Quality standards
* Change requires majority

'''Layer 3: Procedure'''
* Workflow protocols
* Technical standards
* Implementation details
* Change requires consensus

'''Layer 4: Practice'''
* Day-to-day operations
* Individual decisions
* Case-by-case judgments
* Flexible adaptation

=== Entities === ===

'''Epistemic Committee:'''
* Reviews epistemic status changes
* Validates confidence trajectorys
* Resolves disputes
* Membership: Rotating, expertise-based

'''Editorial Board:'''
* Sets editorial policy
* Reviews major changes
* Quality oversight
* Membership: Elected, term-limited

'''Technical Committee:'''
* Maintains infrastructure
* Implements standards
* Security oversight
* Membership: Technical expertise

'''Community Assembly:'''
* General participation
* Proposal submission
* Feedback provision
* Open membership

== Decision-Making Processes ==

=== Process 1: Policy Proposal === ===

# '''Proposal:''' Any member submits proposal
# '''Discussion:''' Community discussion period (7 days)
# '''Revision:''' Proposal refined based on feedback
# '''Voting:''' Voting period (3 days)
# '''Implementation:''' If passed, policy implemented
# '''Review:''' Policy reviewed after 90 days

=== Process 2: Dispute Resolution === ===

# '''Escalation:''' Dispute escalated to committee
# '''Evidence:''' Both parties present evidence
# '''Deliberation:''' Committee reviews (7 days)
# '''Decision:''' Committee issues decision
# '''Appeal:''' Appeal possible to higher committee
# '''Finality:''' Decision binding after appeal period

=== Process 3: Epistemic Review === ===

# '''Request:''' Status change requested
# '''Evidence:''' Evidence presented
# '''Review:''' Committee reviews (14 days)
# '''Calibration:''' Confidence score calibrated
# '''Decision:''' Status assigned
# '''Documentation:''' Rationale documented

== Policies ==

=== Editorial Policy === ===
* Content must be evidence-based
* Epistemic status must be marked
* Sources must be cited
* Logical coherence required

=== Quality Policy === ===
* Minimum standards for publication
* Review requirements
* Upgrade pathways
* Deprecation procedures

=== Inclusion Policy === ===
* Diverse perspectives welcome
* Explicit bias acknowledgment
* No suppression of valid evidence
* Proportional representation

=== Technical Policy === ===
* SMW standards
* Template requirements
* Query optimization
* Security protocols

== Coordination Mechanisms ==

=== Communication === ===
* Public forums for discussion
* Transparent decision records
* Regular status updates
* Feedback channels

=== Conflict Resolution === ===
* Mediation for minor conflicts
* Arbitration for major disputes
* Escalation pathways
* Binding decisions

=== Resource Allocation === ===
* Priority-based allocation
* Evidence of need
* Transparent distribution
* Accountability
